faq.q: Where does a tree grow taller?
faq.a: Only at the tips of its shoots, from buds at the end of each twig. Each spring the buds open and the shoot adds new length.
asks: Does a tree grow from the top?

faq.q: How does a trunk get wider?
faq.a: The cambium, a thin layer under the bark, makes new wood on its inside every year. Each year's wood forms a ring, so the trunk gets thicker.
asks: Why do tree trunks get fatter?

faq.q: Does a carved heart on a tree rise as it grows?
faq.a: No. The trunk does not stretch, so a carving or a nail stays at the same height forever. It may get wider and blurrier as the bark grows around it.
asks: Do branches move up as a tree grows?

faq.a: Outer bark is dead and cannot stretch. As the trunk widens, the old bark splits into cracks and plates while new bark forms underneath.

faq.q: What does a tree build its wood from?
faq.a: From sugar made in its leaves, using carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil. About half the dry weight of wood is carbon taken from the air.

facts: A tree grows taller only at the tips of its shoots; the trunk does not stretch upward.
About half the dry mass of wood is carbon, taken from carbon dioxide in the air.
The growing tissue at shoot and root tips is called a meristem.

quiz.say: A nail is hammered into a tree 1 metre up. Ten years later, how high is it?
quiz.show: A nail is hammered into a tree 1 metre up. Ten years later, how high is it?
quiz.why: The trunk only gets wider, not taller, so the nail stays at the same height.

wrong.1: The trunk does not stretch upward; new height is added only at the tips.
wrong.2: Trees do not pull their trunks down into the soil.
